title: Convo economics lab notebook
content:
Purpose: quick, noisy lab for conversation-oriented unit economics. Not for external consumption — working hypotheses + raw math.

Context / goal:
- Build a lightweight pricing heuristic for conversation-first products (sessions with variable turn lengths, sometimes streaming).
- Surface 2–3 tier prototypes that balance per-user predictability with bursty usage.
- Keep primitives small: tokens, sessions, concurrency, SLA premium.

Assumptions (initial):
- Model baseline = open-6.9B equivalent; hosted cost = $0.000004 per token (net after infra offsets). (Note: placeholder, update with infra-backed numbers).
- Median session = 14 turns, avg 25 tokens per turn => 350 tokens per session.
- Heavy user tail: 95th percentile session = 1,400 tokens.
- Concurrency profile: interactive UX -> many short sessions, occasional long streaming sessions.

Core heuristics to try:
1) Session-banded credits: bucket sessions by expected length (tiny/standard/long) and charge credits per band instead of raw tokens.
2) Elastic per-token with per-session floor: per-token price tiered but minimum floor per session to cover fixed latency/connection overhead.
3) Concurrency-subsidy: users on 'responsive' tier pay a small concurrency premium to subsidize lower latency SLOs.

Quick math snippets:
- Unit costs (rough): token_cost = $0.000004/token, avg_tokens/session = 350 => variable_cost/session = $0.0014.
- Operational overhead (routing, KV cache, infra amortization): assume $0.002/session.
- Support + telemetry allocation: $0.0006/session.
- Total marginal cost/session ≈ $0.004 (rounded).

Tier idea A — "Starter Sessions" (for low freq users):
- 100 free sessions / month (aimed at discovery).
- Overage: $0.05 / session for next 400 sessions, then $0.02 / session at scale (volume discounts).
- Rationale: simplifies billing for non-technical users, hides token complexity.
- Backcalc: $0.05/session -> gross margin per session = $0.046. At 1k monthly sessions, revenue = $50/mo -> covers infra + CAC for small users.

Tier idea B — "Pay-as-you-go (convo)" (token-native):
- $0.003 per 1,000 tokens ($0.000003/token) with a 25-token min per request (so tiny chatter doesn't get free).
- Session floor: $0.01 per session to cover overhead.
- Example: median session (350 tokens) = 350*$0.000003 + $0.01 = $0.01105 -> margin ~0.007/session.
- Pros: tight unit economics, incentivizes efficient prompts. Cons: noisy billing for users.

Tier idea C — "Realtime SLA" (enterprise-ish):
- Base seat price + concurrency guarantee. Example: $150/month per seat includes 1 concurrent session, up to 200k tokens monthly. Additional concurrency slot $50/month.
- Overages: $0.002/token beyond included bundle.
- Add-on: model fallback insurance (auto-failover to cheaper model) at 10% discount if opted-in.

Burst credit model (hybrid):
- Each account accrues "burst credits" proportionate to committed spend or monthly active seats. Credits consumed for sessions above baseline.
- Example: 1 credit ~= 1,000 tokens. Starter plan gives 50 credits/mo. Credits expire in 90 days.

Edge economics: amortized GPU hours -> tokens
- Baseline: 1 GPU-hour can serve ~6M tokens for average workload (batching + streaming mixed).
- If GPU hour cost = $2 (cloud spot blended), per-token infra = $2 / 6,000,000 = $0.000000333 -> good headroom vs token_cost assumption but depends heavily on batch efficiency.
- If batch efficiency dips (small sessions), effective tokens/GPU-hr drops to 1.5M -> infra per-token = $0.000001333.

Experiment matrix (to run with limited telemetry):
- Metric set: ARPU per active user, churn after billshock (30/90 days), variance in monthly cost per user, 95th percentile session cost.
- A/B ideas: session-floor vs pure token; free-session bucket vs credits; explicit concurrency premium vs hidden latency SLO in price.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need precise infra-backed per-token number by model family & region. Ask infra for quantized and fp16 lanes. (Linked: GH-PR-2345).
- How to present session floors in billing UI without confusing engineering users? Try an "estimated cost" preview on the console.
- Small-sys edge: rate-limit + credits interplay when users open many tiny connections.
- Behavioral: do users optimize prompt length if given per-token bills? historical evidence noisy. Consider gentle UX nudges before price shocks.

Quick scenarios (sensitivity):
1) If token cost halves (better kernels / spot buys) -> payg token tier becomes very attractive; session-floor can be lowered mid-experiment.
2) If tail sessions dominate infra (95th percentile chewing up capacity) -> introduce 'long-session surcharge' or encourage chunking via SDK patterns.

Short list of actionable next steps (this doc owner):
- Request stable infra token-cost matrix from infra (per-model, per-region) by 2025-03-07.
- Spin two billing mockups: (A) session-bands UI, (B) token-native with session floor — usability quick test with 5 internal devs. Due 2025-03-14.
- Prototype credit accumulation rules in billing sandbox (simulate churn impact).

Random scribbles / scribbled formulas:
- per_session_margin ≈ price_session - (token_cost*avg_tokens + infra_overhead + ops_alloc).
- k-session-decay model for credits: credits_t+1 = credits_t * (1 - k) + accrual. Try k=0.08 as starting point.

Notes-to-self: keep presentation clear: engineers like tokens, product managers like sessions. Offer both: session-bands (default) + advanced token view (console).

End of notebook (will tidy into sketch doc once infra numbers land).
